edges.description: CCDC62 localises to the developing acrosome and interacts with GOPC, a Golgi protein required for proacrosomal vesicle transport; without CCDC62 acrosome formation is disrupted.
Failure of acrosome biogenesis produces round-headed, acrosome-less sperm.
Acrosome-less, dysmorphic sperm cannot fertilise the oocyte in vivo.
CCDC62 loss disrupts acrosome formation in spermatids, with deformed sperm, the mechanism proposed for the human disease.
edges.limitations: The human phenotype rests on a single proband; mouse spermiogenesis defects may be more complete than the human presentation, and acrosome ultrastructure was not compared directly across species.

nodes.description: The repro29 ENU line carries a nonsense mutation in Ccdc62 exon 6 producing a truncated protein. Homozygous males are infertile with deformed, poorly motile sperm. A complementation cross with a CRISPR Ccdc62 knockout confirms that the infertility is caused by the Ccdc62 mutation.

The human phenotype is globozoospermia, round-headed sperm lacking a normal acrosome. The proband was ascertained from a globozoospermia cohort and the CCDC62 nonsense variant was identified as its likely cause.

nodes.description: Loss of CCDC62 disrupts formation of the acrosome during spermiogenesis, producing malformed spermatids. The acrosome is the Golgi-derived cap over the sperm head; its failure yields round-headed (globozoospermic) sperm.
